name: Zack D Studio
description: Zack D Studio turns one question into a short curiosity-loop video: it writes a script, makes 3D character sheets, keyframe images and Veo video clips, and assembles a final cut with optional voice-over, music and burned-in captions.
shortDescription: One question to a finished short video: script, characters, keyframes, clips and final cut.
fullDescription: You type a topic or question (or pick one of the seed ideas or a template). The action button then follows the pipeline step by step: Write script, Approve script, Generate character sheets, Generate keyframes, Animate clips, and Render final cut. You can edit the script beats before approving. Each paid step asks for confirmation first and any failed item can be retried with Redo. The final cut is assembled in your browser, and you can add a voice-over, background music and AI captions, then download the MP4 or the captions as an .srt file. Finished work is kept in a History sidebar.
bestFor: Creators who want a short explainer or story video from a single question without writing a script or storyboard themselves.
whenToUse: You have a question or topic and want a short narrated-style video about it.
You want consistent 3D-style characters across the shots of a video.
You want to start from a ready-made template instead of a blank project.
You want captions burned into a finished video.
whenToUseAnother: Use Video Studio (#/video) to generate a single clip from a prompt.
Use Storyboard (#/storyboard) to plan shots without generating the whole video.
Use Timeline (#/timeline) to edit footage you already have.
keyFeatures: Pipeline button that changes with the step: Write script, Approve script, Generate character sheets, Generate keyframes, Animate clips, Render final cut.
Editable script beats with an approval step before anything paid is generated.
Look picker, voice picker and extras such as a consistency boost, voice-over and music.
Templates: one tap loads an upstream template; loading one never calls a paid API.
Redo on any character sheet, keyframe or clip, and a message when part of a batch fails.
Final cut assembled in the browser; Download MP4 and Download captions (.srt).
Burn captions with a chosen language and theme (asks for confirmation about the cost).
History sidebar and a New project button.

featureExplanations.explanation: One button whose label shows the next step. Click it to run that step; it shows Working while a step runs.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: You do not need to find the next step yourself.

featureExplanations.explanation: The script is shown as editable beat cards. Approving it locks in the plan so character sheets, keyframes and clips can be generated.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Fix the story before paying for images and video.

featureExplanations.explanation: Loads an upstream template: a script only, or a finished project with script, keyframes and clips.
featureExplanations.whyToUse: Start quickly or see how a finished project looks.

featureExplanations.explanation: Adds AI captions to the final video after you confirm a cost warning (about $0.20 minimum, $0.005 per second).

howToUse: 1. Open Zack D Studio from the side menu (#/zackd). 2. Type a question or topic, or pick a seed idea or template. 3. Click 'Write script' and edit the beats if you like. 4. Click 'Approve script'. 5. Click the next button to generate character sheets, then keyframes, then 'Animate clips' (the most expensive step, it asks first). 6. Optionally add voice-over and music. 7. Click 'Render final cut'. 8. Download the MP4, download the .srt, or burn captions. Use Redo to retry any failed item and New project to start again.
howToSteps: Type a topic or pick a template.
Edit the beats and click Approve script.
Generate character sheets (when needed), then keyframes.
Download the MP4 or captions, or burn captions into the video.
gettingStarted: Start from a template to see the whole flow without paying for generation.
Keep your first topic short and specific.
Approve the script only when you are happy with it.

inputDetails.name: Topic
inputDetails.description: The question or subject of the video.
inputDetails.whenToUse: Always, unless you load a template.

generationModes: Pipeline (script, character sheets, keyframes, clips, final cut)

modeExplanations.description: Each step runs only when you click the action button and confirm paid steps.

modelCapabilities: Images and clips are generated through the app's video and image models (clips use Veo 3.1 according to the confirmation text). Exact model options per step are not listed here.
outputs: Optional captioned video saved to the library
limitations: Clip generation is the most expensive step and asks for confirmation.
A step with failures can be retried with Redo; the project keeps what succeeded.
The final cut is assembled in the browser, so very long projects depend on your device.

limitationDetails.impact: Character sheets, keyframes, clips and caption burning use credits.
limitationDetails.workaround: Use a template or Redo only what failed.

troubleshooting: Message like '1 of 2 failed: ... Use Redo to retry them.': click Redo on the failed items.
Generate stays disabled: type a topic first.

steps: Read the message under the prompt bar.
Click Redo on the failed character sheet, keyframe or clip.

commonProblems.whyItHappens: The script has not been approved yet.
commonProblems.howToFix: Review the beats and click Approve script.

steps: Render final cut and download the MP4.

faqs.question: What does Zack D Studio make?
faqs.answer: A short video built from one question: script, 3D characters, keyframes, clips and a final cut.

faqs.question: Can I try it without paying?
faqs.answer: Loading a template never calls a paid API, so you can explore the flow first.

glossary.Keyframe: The still image a clip starts from.
glossary.Character sheet: A reference image that keeps a character consistent across shots.

tips: Edit the script before approving it.
Download the final cut right away.
bestPractices: Check the script, then generate images, then clips, so the costly step comes last.
